title: NVDA Stock Edges Down On DOJ Interest In $12.9 Billion Hugging Face Acquisition - Stocktwits
content: Shares of Nvidia Corp (NVDA) slipped 1% on Wednesday  following reports that the U.S. Department of Justice has inquired about how its planned acquisition of Hugging Face could affect competition in artificial intelligence. According to a report from Reuters, citing people familiar with the matter, department officials have asked whether the Hugging Face deal would allow Nvidia to control a key distribution point for AI models and tools. The questioning adds to the years-long probe by antitrust regulators on Nvidia’s conduct, which kicked off under former President Joe Biden, the report said. The probe is reportedly continuing with no indication that current President Donald Trump has any involvement. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has a relationship with Trump and recently joined the President on his diplomatic trip to China. The DOJ’s recent line of questioning covers the company’s acquisitions, investments, sales practices, and whether it has pressured customers, sources told Reuters. As part of the probe, the DOJ has reportedly examined Nvidia’s other acquisition deals, including the December 2025 deal to buy SchedMD, sources told Reuters. The department has also scrutinized Nvidia's conduct following other transactions, including its licensing deal with chip startup Groq and its acquisition of Run.ai, the report added. Nvidia announced in early September that it had agreed to buy Hugging Face for approximately $12.93 billion. The transaction includes roughly $11.9 billion payable to Hugging Face’s investors and an equity-based retention program of up to about $1 billion for employees who join Nvidia. Hugging Face operates a widely used platform that hosts millions of open-source AI models, datasets, and applications, serving millions of developers and hundreds of thousands of companies. It is often described as a central hub for open AI development. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has pledged that the platform will remain open to models, frameworks, clouds, and computing platforms from across the industry, and that Nvidia’s own chips will not be required to use it. The deal is expected to close in the first half of 2027. (ORCL) share price rallied about 11% on Wednesday, closing its best day since May this year, after executives unveiled a net cash-flow-positive outlook, helping alleviate capex concerns. ORCL stock has been under pressure so far this year amid mounting concerns that ballooning debt loads and high interest rates would make the tech titan's heavy AI investments unsustainable. Chief Financial Officer Hilary Maxson announced that Oracle expects to achieve $30 billion in free cash flow by the fiscal year ending in May 2029 at its investor day in Las Vegas. The forecast heavily outperformed Wall Street expectations, as data compiled by Bloomberg and FactSet indicated that analysts anticipated the metric to remain deeply negative during that period. Fueling the optimism is a robust revenue trajectory. Oracle reaffirmed its target of $225 billion in total revenue by fiscal 2030, signaling an average annual growth rate of roughly 35%. Operating margins are projected to climb past 40% by the end of the decade. To manage the heavy capital expenditures required for the build-out, Oracle outlined a disciplined funding strategy, which included a pledge to limit total additional funding needs between fiscal 2027 and 2030 to $20 billion, split evenly between equity and debt. The company is executing a massive data center build-out to support major clients like OpenAI, stepping into direct competition with established hyperscalers like Amazon (AMZN) and Google (GOOGL). Maxson noted that Oracle plans to deliver an additional seven gigawatts of data center capacity over the next couple of years, pushing its total fleet capacity beyond 10 gigawatts by the conclusion of fiscal 2028. To put the scale in perspective, a single gigawatt of electricity generates enough power for about 750,000 U.S. homes at once. While Oracle hit negative $23.7 billion cash flow in the fiscal year ending May 2026 due to infrastructure costs, executives emphasized that capital expenditures will peak through the current and upcoming fiscal years before declining significantly in fiscal 2029. Shares of Hims & Hers (HIMS) jumped 5% on Wednesday after the Department of Health and Human Services said it would temporarily allow compounding pharmacies to produce six popular peptides. HHS said it will not go after state-licensed pharmacies, federal facilities, or licensed doctors for compounding six peptides—BPC-157, Epitalon, KPV, MOTS-c, Semax, and TB-500—as long as they follow basic rules on ingredient quality, manufacturing, safety reporting, labeling, and prescriptions written for individual patients. “...based on the Pharmacy Compounding Advisory Committee (PCAC) meeting and data regarding utilization of peptides, HHS believes that there is significant interest in the use of these peptides in compounding,” HHS said, referring to the advisory committee recommendation in July that some peptides be considered for compounding. The new policy is temporary while the FDA completes formal rulemaking on the official list of bulk substances that can be used in compounding. Compounders must report serious adverse events with the use of the drugs or any product quality issues such as contamination to the FDA, HHS added.  Compounded drugs are not FDA-approved. Hims has already prepared for a potential approval of peptide compounding by securing a California peptide facility and testing ingredients, while signaling interest in offering items such as sermorelin, glutathione, and NAD+ depending on final regulatory outcomes. Peptides used for recovery, inflammation, sleep, and related wellness goals have drawn strong consumer interest online, even without formal FDA approval. “We have spent years building the infrastructure we need in our very own US-based peptide manufacturing facility, developing dosing protocols with clinical experts, and setting up frameworks to better understand these emerging treatments,” the company’s Chief Medical Officer Anant Vinjamoori said after the HHS directive in a post on X. HIMS CEO Andrew Dudum also termed it “encouraging progress.” HIMS, however, has also faced setbacks this year, including an FTC lawsuit filed in late July alleging deceptive privacy practices involving data sharing with advertising platforms and misleading billing or cancellation practices. The company transitioned from offering compounded GLP-1s to branded versions earlier this year, pressuring margins despite subscriber growth. Shares of gene-editing companies, including Prime Medicine (PRME), rallied on Wednesday after the U.S. Food and Drug Administration issued draft guidance designed to speed personalized treatment for rare genetic diseases. Under the FDA’s new draft guidance, companies can file one application that covers several versions of the same gene-editing treatment, as long as each version aims to make the same kind of genetic correction. Once clinical results support the core approach, new versions that stay within set limits can be added later using mainly lab tests instead of full new patient trials. The guidance applies to gene-editing therapies for rare diseases caused by a single known genetic fault. Companies with modular gene editing platforms stand to benefit most, including Prime Medicine’s prime-editing system and lipid-nanoparticle delivery, if the draft is adopted. The draft guidance is now open for public comment, which will be later reviewed by the FDA before it decides whether to adopt it. Shares of Prime Medicine were up 20% at the time of writing, while Beam Therapeutics traded 14% higher and Intellia Therapeutics (NTLA) and Editas Medicine (EDIT) climbed 6-11%. CRISPR Therapeutics (CRSP) posted more modest gains of 4%. Prime clocked larger gains than its peers as it builds on company-specific updates. Earlier this month, the company announced it had dosed the first patient in a global Phase 1/2 trial of PM577a for Wilson disease—the first known use of prime editing therapy inside a living patient. The FDA also granted the program Rare Pediatric Disease designation. Initial clinical data from the Wilson disease study are expected in 2027. The company also recently received the FDA’s clearance to start human trials of an alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency candidate. The Federal Reserve opted to keep its target interest rate steady on Wednesday, but financial markets focused on Chair Kevin Warsh's announcement of a structural shift in the frequency of future interest rate decisions. The central bank held interest rates steady at 3.75% to 4% amid elevated inflation and a strong job market. The Federal Open Market Committee approved the following statement for release by a 10–2 vote. This move comes as the Fed pivots its attention to inflation amid energy price fluctuations from the conflict in Iran, while the job market remains resilient. “Inflation remains elevated,” the Fed statement said. “The accumulation of more information will help the Committee determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the Committee’s 2 percent goal. The Committee will deliver price stability.” Governors Lisa D. Cook and Beth M. Hammack preferred to raise the target range for the federal funds rate by a quarter percentage point at this meeting. Under Warsh’s revamped framework, the FOMC will issue rate decisions at seven of its eight scheduled sessions in 2027, reserving one meeting exclusively for broad monetary policy strategy without issuing a formal rate statement. By 2028, the central bank plans to reduce its rate-setting votes to six per year, leaving two gatherings devoted entirely to strategic evaluations. Warsh—who assumed the chairmanship in May—explained that spacing out policy decisions allows more economic data to accumulate while giving policymakers dedicated time to address broader structural issues. He noted that effective policy requires balancing short-term economic monitoring with longer-horizon strategic deliberations. Short-term two-year yields initially moved higher by up to five basis points immediately after officials opted to pause, as investors absorbed the 10–2 vote. However, short-dated yields reversed course once Warsh discussed the calendar restructuring during his press conference. The yield on the two-year Treasury note—highly sensitive to near-term policy expectations—dropped as much as four basis points to 4.7% as traders interpreted the schedule modifications as a dovish signal. In contrast, long-term Treasury yields remained elevated, with the 10-year yield hovering above the 5% level. With a market cap of about $5.3 trillion, Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA) is the largest company in the world -- and it's easy to see how it reached that size. The tech giant's advanced processors are the dominant compute hardware in the data centers that underpin the entire generative artificial intelligence (AI) industry, and as soaring demand for its chips continues to outstrip supply, it enjoys booming sales at sky-high margins. That said, all investors know that past performance doesn't guarantee future results. And the larger a company becomes, the harder it is for additional growth to move the needle on its finances. So what might this leading tech stock be worth by the end of 2027? Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue » It's been roughly four years since OpenAI's ChatGPT introduced the world to the power of generative AI, and the revolution that it triggered shows no signs of slowing down. According to analysts at Goldman Sachs, tech companies' AI-related capital expenditures will total more than $1 trillion in 2026. And much of that spending will go toward graphics processing units (GPUs) and other data center compute hardware created by companies like Nvidia. The supply of advanced semiconductor equipment remains tight relative to demand, and Nvidia's GPUs remain the most popular data center AI accelerators, a situation that allows it to charge high prices. These persistent tailwinds were reflected in the company's second-quarter earnings. Revenue jumped 106% year over year to $96.2 billion, driven mostly by strength in the company's data center segment, which grew 117%. This business involves designing and selling advanced AI infrastructure. And management plans to keep the momentum going with new releases, such as its Vera Rubin platform, which is designed specifically to handle agentic AI workloads. Nvidia's bottom line is also looking good; the company's net income jumped 32% year over year to $59.7 billion in the period. On the surface, Nvidia looks like the perfect stock to own. But investors should be aware that it faces some big challenges. Perhaps the biggest is its lack of diversification. In the past, Nvidia boasted a broader business model as it sold GPUs for consumer video games, machine learning, cryptocurrency mining, virtual reality devices, and data centers, among other uses. However, the mix of end-uses has condensed dramatically: Data centers now account for over 90% of its revenue. This situation leaves Nvidia exceptionally exposed to a potential downturn in the AI market. And even the bulls should be willing to accept that the current levels of data center spending probably won't last forever. A recent paper by Columbia University finance professor Stijn Van Nieuwerburgh (first presented at the nonpartisan Brookings Institution) concludes that U.S. businesses and consumers will eventually have to spend the equivalent of 9% of the country's GDP on AI-related services to justify the current levels of capital investment going toward the technology. That's as much as we spend on food, and far more than we spend on essentials like energy and construction. While large language models (LLMs) are useful, they are notoriously difficult to monetize due to their huge energy consumption and the intense level of competition in the space, especially from lower-cost Chinese alternatives. In fact, industry leader Anthropic reported an eye-popping net loss of $80 billion in the first half of 2026. If the consumer-facing side of the AI market struggles to turn a profit, that could eventually lead to a smaller market for hardware providers like Nvidia. Trading today at a forward price-to-earnings (P/E) multiple of 23.5, Nvidia stock is still relatively cheap relative to its growth potential. And investors who believe the AI boom will maintain its momentum can comfortably expect the stock to offer additional multibagger returns from here. That said, this represents the best-case scenario. And there are several reasons to be less optimistic. The AI industry shows many of the signs that it's in an unsustainable bubble. And Nvidia's business model isn't diversified enough to be cushioned against the painful impact of a spending slowdown. With these risks in mind, it looks more likely to me that when we get to the end of 2027, Nvidia shares will be trading close to flat compared to their price today. title: Nvidia Stock Is 10% Below Its Record. Does Anthropic's IPO Filing Make It a Buy? - The Motley Fool
content: How much of the Claude maker's rent goes to the chip giant? Anthropic made its initial public offering (IPO) filing public on Monday, showing what the Claude maker has agreed to pay to rent computing power built on Nvidia (NVDA -1.18%) chips. Deals with three providers have a price tag: up to $120.5 billion with SpaceXAI, an arm of SpaceX (SPCX -2.25%), around $44.6 billion with Nscale, and about $41.3 billion with Lambda. All told, that's up to about $206 billion. But they're rental contracts with cloud providers, not chip orders, and the same filing commits even more money to computing on Google's chips. Nvidia shares were up about 2% on Monday as of this writing, at around $216 -- still about 10% below their Oct. 6 record close. I think the filing says less about Nvidia's future sales than that $206 billion suggests. The biggest part mainly rents capacity that's already built, or will be by December. In May, Anthropic said it would use all the capacity at SpaceX's Colossus 1 data center, which has over 220,000 Nvidia graphics processing units (GPUs), including older H100 and H200 chips. By late May, the deal also covered capacity at SpaceX's newer Colossus 2 site. Hardware that must be running by December is mostly already sold, or shipping now. When the full SpaceXAI capacity arrives, the rent runs around $3.1 billion a month. But those contracts are also the easiest to exit. After their initial lock-in periods end in early 2027, either side can cancel with 90 days' notice. The Nscale and Lambda deals look more like new demand, as that capacity still needs to be built. But Nscale must use its best efforts to line up financing for the Nvidia GPUs and the data center infrastructure. And Lambda's biggest agreement, around $34.9 billion, can be canceled if Lambda doesn't secure its facility lease in time. Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue » Of course, rent pays for more than chips. It also covers the buildings, the power, the financing, and the provider's profit. So Nvidia's share of the $206 billion is likely much smaller. Anthropic also committed at least $44.9 billion to Microsoft through May 2033, but didn't say how much of that runs on Nvidia chips. A July supply deal with Advanced Micro Devices for its Helios rack-scale systems could also top $20 billion if Anthropic takes its full initial capacity. Anthropic agreed to spend at least around $114.5 billion with Alphabet's (GOOGL +1.34%)(GOOG +1.60%) Google through July 2033, and it estimates that extra computing on Google's tensor processing units (TPUs) from 2028 to 2031 could cost between $125 billion and $150 billion. Its leases with Broadcom (AVGO +2.77%) for TPU-based hardware total around $161.2 billion in rent. Amazon, which makes its own Trainium chips, gets a commitment of at least $110.0 billion. Put another way, Google and Broadcom alone account for about $276 billion, leaving out the extra TPU estimate. Unlike the SpaceXAI deals, these commitments can't be canceled except in narrow cases, like a default or the other side's uncured breach. Anthropic's revenue soared to $16.3 billion in the first half of 2026 from $1.2 billion a year before. But it's steering more of its committed money to Google's chips than to Nvidia's. For the second quarter of fiscal 2027 (the three months ended July 26, 2026), Nvidia's data center business (home to its AI chips and systems) had revenue of $89.0 billion, over twice the year-ago total. That followed $75.2 billion in fiscal Q1 and $62.3 billion in fiscal Q4 2026, so the business has been adding roughly $13 billion or more every quarter. At that latest rate, the business takes in about $356 billion a year. Anthropic's full SpaceXAI rent runs about $37 billion a year, and just some of that flows to Nvidia. "This time last year, one lab alone was driving the buildout," CEO Jensen Huang said in Nvidia's fiscal Q2 earnings release. Now, he said, "multiple frontier labs" are "scaling in parallel." After all, investors aren't paying much for that growth. At around $216, Nvidia stock trades at about 14 times the earnings per share analysts expect for its fiscal 2028 (its year ending January 2028). Broadcom, in comparison, goes for about 17 times the earnings expected in its next fiscal year. So, is Nvidia stock a buy after Anthropic's filing? The $206 billion number overstates what's headed Nvidia's way, and Google's chips are winning more of Anthropic's commitments. But Nvidia's growth doesn't rest on any one lab, and its valuation arguably already assumes growth will slow sharply. I'd consider buying Nvidia stock at about $216. The filing just doesn't do much for that case by itself. title: Nvidia’s New $3 Billion AI Bet Is on One of Its Own Customers - The Motley Fool
content: Nvidia’s $3 billion investment in Meta strengthens an important partnership. It also raises familiar questions about who is funding the AI boom. Nvidia (NVDA -1.18%) announced this morning that it plans to invest $3 billion in Meta Platforms (META -1.24%), one of its biggest customers. Nvidia will make the investment as part of Meta's recently announced stock offering. The companies said they will expand their work on Muse, Meta's popular AI assistant, working to improve Meta's family of models that power it. That technical partnership aims to improve both training -- building an AI model -- and inference, using the model after it's been trained. Meta said it plans to expand its deployment of Nvidia's latest hardware: Vera Rubin GPU systems, Vera CPUs, and networking technology. The companies also said they are considering working on tools that would help AI agents operate securely as well as help monitor their behavior, but those discussions are still exploratory and nothing has been agreed upon. This is a deepening of an already close relationship. While we don't know where exactly Meta ranks, it was very likely already one of Nvidia's biggest customers, and in February, Meta said it would deploy millions of Nvidia's Blackwell and Vera Rubin GPUs, along with CPUs and networking equipment. And given the lack of detail in this announcement, it makes it a little hard to tell how much new business Nvidia is actually getting here. Meta says it will use more of its hardware, but the announcement doesn't say how much more or what those additional purchases will be worth. And their engineers were already working together, so the technical partnership sounds like an extension of work they were already doing. Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue » More than three years into the AI boom, Nvidia is still going strong. Last quarter, the company's top-line reached $96.2 billion, more than double what it recorded a year earlier. Operating profit grew a whopping 124% to $63.7 billion. It's easy to take this for granted at this point, but those really are simply incredible growth numbers for a company of this size. Unsurprisingly, Nvidia's data center business accounted for more than 90% of sales. While that is precisely what's fueling the company's rapid growth, it means Nvidia's fate is directly tied to the rest of the AI industry. Nvidia -- or rather, its stock price -- cannot afford to have the AI capex spend slow. The deal made today makes sense. Meta needs capital, and Nvidia is flush with cash. A $3 billion infusion gives Nvidia an appreciating asset -- Meta stock -- while ensuring a major customer continues to purchase its hardware. This is one of many such deals that, while completely above-board, have raised concerns over whether Nvidia is using its considerable balance sheet to paper over cracks in a less-than-healthy AI ecosystem. I think there's something to these claims, though I would caution investors to read too much into a deal like this. The reality is, Nvidia has a whole lot of cash on hand and needs to do something with it. Meta stock is a reasonable place to deploy that capital. title: Nvidia Stock Is Down 12% From Its High. Here's What History Says Happens Next. - The Motley Fool
content: Nvidia looks dirt cheap from a historical standpoint. Nvidia (NVDA -1.18%) has had a rough few weeks. While it notched a new all-time high at the start of October, the stock has sold off and is now down over 10% from that level. That's a notable sell-off, especially given that it's the world's largest company by market cap. But is it the perfect buying opportunity right now? Let's take a look at what history says to find out. Nvidia may have been available to invest in for nearly three decades, but its current business state has only been relevant since 2023, when the AI arms race began. If you look at a stock chart that uses the starting price of 2023 as the high point for Nvidia and then look at drops after that, you can see that selling off 10% or more is nothing new. In fact, it appears that Nvidia spends about as much time 10% or more off its all-time high as it does near its all-time high. So, this is familiar territory for Nvidia investors. The question is, is it a buy now? I think the best way to assess this is to look at Nvidia's valuation. The best way to assess Nvidia's stock is the forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio, which uses analyst estimates to determine what its earnings over this fiscal year will be. From this perspective, Nvidia is extremely cheap, but there's one glaring thing that hasn't happened yet. Normally, Nvidia's stock rallies to a 40-times forward earnings level by year-end. It hasn't done that this year, and if it did, that would roughly result in the stock doubling. I doubt that happens, but the market is essentially not pricing in any 2027 growth, which is a huge oversight. Nvidia has already announced to investors that it expects to deliver nearly 90% year-over-year revenue growth for the upcoming quarter. This is far greater than many big tech stocks and will likely lead to a strong stock performance next year. None of this seems to be priced in because Nvidia trades at such a low forward P/E ratio. To put its 22.7 times forward earnings price tag in perspective, the S&P 500 (^GSPC +0.28%) trades for 19.2 times forward earnings. That means Nvidia is barely getting a premium over the broader market despite telling investors it will nearly double revenue in the next quarter. That's a huge arbitrage opportunity, and investors should use this sell-off to scoop up shares. title: Nvidia Just Announced Plans to Pour Billions Into Meta's Muse - The Motley Fool
content: The chipmaker and social media titan are deepening their partnership. When Meta Platforms (META -1.24%) released its quarterly report last week, it contained more than the usual financial information. The social media and artificial intelligence (AI) purveyor announced plans to create a new class of stock -- Class C shares. This non-voting stock, which is poised to begin trading early next year, will be used primarily to raise capital for its soaring AI expenses, employee compensation, and to fund potential acquisitions. Meta plans to effect a 2-for-1 stock split on Jan. 19, 2027 -- in the form of a stock dividend -- issuing one share of Class C stock to shareholders of record for each share of Class A or Class B common stock they own. Perhaps as importantly, Meta announced plans to raise a total of $95 billion to backstop its heavy investments in AI -- and the move is attracting backing from some of the biggest names in technology. Chief among them is Nvidia (NVDA -1.18%), arguably the architect of the AI revolution. Just this morning, the semiconductor specialist announced plans to pour billions of dollars into Meta to fund its AI ambitions. In a separate press release that dropped on Monday, Nvidia and Meta announced plans to expand their collaboration on the Muse family of AI models, citing the growing popularity and demand for AI agents. Indeed, Meta's Muse models and AI agents, powered by Nvidia processors, have "delivered frontier-level benchmark performance and surging consumer downloads since launch," according to the release. The pair plan to deepen their collaboration, "by partnering on optimizations across workflows to maximize performance and improve total cost of ownership." Nvidia and Meta are also exploring other opportunities, including the use of Nvidia's OpenShell and Sentry, designed to ensure the safe deployment and monitoring of AI agent behavior. Meta also plans to increase its deployment of Nvidia's Vera Rubin graphics processing units (GPUs), Vera CPUs, and Spectrum-X Ethernet to boost the performance of its AI agents, Meta is already one of Nvidia's biggest customers. The pair expanded their partnership earlier this year, announcing a multi-year deal in which Meta would deploy "millions" of Nvidia's Blackwell and Rubin chips, as well as the company's Grace and Vera CPUs. Meta's fundraising efforts will be spread out over the coming months. First, the company will raise $35 billion through an underwritten public offering, attracting foundational investors such as Nvidia, Advanced Micro Devices, and Broadcom. The trio of AI chipmakers have expressed interest in buying up to $5 billion in Meta's Class A shares, with Nvidia contributing $3 billion. Meta plans to raise another $60 billion through the sale of Class C shares beginning early next year. The fundraising binge comes at a critical time for the tech giant. Meta recently confirmed that it is on track to have 2026 capital expenditures in the range of $135 billion to $145 billion, roughly double the $72.2 billion the company spent last year. Concerns about the company's legal challenges and heavy spending on AI have weighed on Meta, which has shed 16% over the past year. However, at 21 times earnings, the stock has much of the downside potential priced in. For its part, Nvidia continues to post year-over-year revenue and profit growth of more than 100%, yet is selling for less than 28 times earnings. Despite the risk of a potential slowdown in AI-related spending, both of these industry titans are attractively priced. Danny Vena, CPA has positions in Broadcom, Meta Platforms, and Nvidia. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang described the objectives of the expanded relationship in a company statement. "NVIDIA and Meta are expanding our partnership to optimize the computing infrastructure end to end for capable, efficient and secure AI agents," Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said in a statement. The expanded agreement follows the launch of Meta's Muse artificial intelligence models and associated AI agents. The companies intend to collaborate on further improvements to the training and inference capabilities of the Muse models. title: Nvidia Picks Up $3B Stock In Meta's Equity Offering, Will Help Improve Muse AI Platform - Stocktwits
content: Nvidia Corp (NVDA) said early Tuesday that it is investing $3 billion in Meta Platforms’ (META) equity offering and will partner with the social media giant to improve its Muse AI agentic platform. Meta announced a massive $97.5 billion equity offering on Monday and said later in the day that it sold $12.5 billion of preferred shares at $50 apiece and $25 billion of common stock at $625 per share. The offer includes about $60 billion in an at-the-market share sale program, including the company’s planned Class C nonvoting shares. Meta said earlier that Nvidia, Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), and Broadcom (AVGO) had agreed to buy as much as $5 billion of the common shares in aggregate. Meta intends to use the proceeds to support its investment in AI infrastructure and its consumer AI tools. NVDA stock was down 0.6% in overnight trading ahead of Tuesday, while META shares were flat. Large-cap tech names were mixed following Anthropic’s IPO filing, although some memory stocks eked out gains in overnight and Asian trading. “NVIDIA and Meta today announced they will partner to expand their work on Muse and the Muse family of models to improve inference and training performance, reflecting popular demand for useful AI agents,” the AI chipmaker said in a press release. The two will work to optimize workflows to maximize Muse’s performance and improve total cost of ownership, and consider additional collaboration opportunities, specifically around Nvidia’s OpenShell Reference Architecture. In February, Meta and Nvidia announced a multi-year partnership covering millions of AI GPUs, CPUs and networking technology. They did not reveal the financial details for the deal. Meta’s equity offering follows similar ones by Alphabet (GOOGL) and Intel Corp (INTC) earlier this year – rare moves by the cash-rich companies. During its earnings report last week, Meta announced a new class of nonvoting stock that could ultimately fund acquisitions and other expenses. The so-called Class C stock will be distributed to existing investors through a stock dividend and will start trading in January 2027. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment for META shifted to ‘bullish’ on Tuesday, down from ‘extremely bullish’ the previous day, while sentiment for NVDA remained ‘bullish.’ Trader views on Meta’s offering were mixed and several were holding off for quarterly reports from hyperscalers Alphabet (GOOGL), Microsoft (MSFT) and Amazon (AMZN) later this week to form a position on the stock. META shares are down 4.2% year to date, while the NVDA stock has gained 16%. For updates and corrections, email newsroom[at]stocktwits[dot]com. Comments posted here will also appear on symbol pages. Memory stocks rose after Anthropic’s IPO filing, with gains spreading to Asian markets as investors weighed the AI company’s surging revenue and compute commitments alongside its large losses. Micron (MU) stock rose 1% in overnight trading ahead of Tuesday, while Seoul shares of SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics gained 5.6% and 4%, respectively, on Tuesday. South Korea’s Kospi was up 3% at the time of writing. Earlier, the Korea Exchange triggered a “sidecar,” a brief pause in program trading that kicks in when futures move sharply. The Direxion Daily South Korea Bull 3X ETF (KORU) rose 2.8% in overnight trading. Neocloud stocks also recovered, with CoreWeave (CRWV) and Nebius (NBIS) gaining about 0.5% each overnight, while cloud giant Alphabet (GOOGL) was up 0.3%. Nvidia (NVDA), Intel (INTC), Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), Amazon (AMZN) and Microsoft (MSFT) were in the red after gains in Monday’s regular session. Anthropic made its S-1 filing public on Monday, showing first-half revenue of $16.3 billion, up from $1.16 billion in H1 2025. The company reported a net loss of $80.7 billion, largely driven by a $72.4 billion accounting charge related to convertible notes. However, Anthropic’s long-term purchase commitments, which flow through to cloud and AI infrastructure providers, caught investors’ attention. The AI company would spend $450 billion in cloud computing agreements over the next seven to ten years, The Wall Street Journal reported, citing the filing. It plans to spend $111 billion on Google cloud computing contracts, $110 billion with Amazon Web Services, and $31 billion on Microsoft, “regardless of actual usage.” Anthropic will also spend up to $86 billion renting Nvidia chips from smaller AI cloud providers Nscale and Lambda through 2033 and 2034, respectively, in addition to other cloud deals, the Journal reported. Anthropic’s financials drew broadly positive comments from analysts and investors, with some praising its pace of growth and deep customer spread. Anthropic will go public on the Nasdaq exchange under the ticker symbol "ANT," according to the S-1. The company reportedly plans to list its shares in the week of Nov. 16, the Journal reported separately, citing people familiar with the matter. The Federal Reserve is set to meet for its October policy decision on Tuesday, with markets overwhelmingly expecting the central bank to hold rates steady after a 25-basis-point hike at its previous meeting. Morgan Stanley’s chief U.S. economist Michael Gapen agrees with the market, saying that while the Fed will hold rates in October, markets should still expect the policy rate to rise later. In an interview with CNBC, Gapen said that even if the Fed holds rates steady this month, “the Fed's (not) out of the water by any means,” adding that he doesn’t “think they (the Fed) think that” either. Gapen believes the Fed will cite a wait-and-see approach, saying it will watch underlying trends to assess where policy may ultimately go. “So I think that's the balance. They stay on hold,” but with the expectation of policy rates going higher in the future. According to data from the CME FedWatch tool, markets are placing the odds of a ‘Hold’ decision at 88.9%, significantly up from 35.8% a month ago. Meanwhile, the probability of a rate hike of up to 50 bps is 81.6%, according to the website. Gapen thinks the central bank could argue that it will choose how to validate the market’s financial conditions that are tightening. He said, “One argument against going at successive meetings would be the risk of causing too much tightening in financial conditions.” However, he added that there are risks to whichever way the Fed goes, but it would likely take a “more gradual pace.” The economist agreed that the war in the Middle East and rising oil prices would pose a risk to inflation, adding that Morgan Stanley is “factoring some of it into our inflation forecast next year” and that the Federal Open Market Committee will likely consider it as well. The bigger question is whether the central bank can afford to hike benchmark interest rates every other meeting and assess data as it comes, adding that energy markets will likely dictate that course. “I think it's right to think the economy can handle 75 to 100 basis points in total hikes without, without, say, a tremendous amount of concern,” about impact on yields, Gapen said, but cautioned that if the Fed needs to do six or seven total hikes to get back to 2023 levels, then it could cause some concerns. U.S. Antimony based its estimates on gold priced at $4,000 per ounce and antimony at $8.30 per pound. Within the measured and indicated category, the company estimates that the deposit contains antimony valued at $233.9 million and gold worth $79.9 million. U.S. Antimony purchased the Nolan Creek Bureau of Land Management claims at a public trustee sale on Jan. 30. It subsequently expanded its holdings by acquiring additional Alaska state claims to cover more of the surrounding mineralized area. Work began in October, and a contractor was tasked with extracting an exploratory bulk sample weighing about 1,000 tons. "This is another example of USAC's "fast track" approach to mining methods. This shipment will represent our first antimony delivered from our exploration efforts in Alaska to Montana for processing,” said Gary C. Evans, Chairman and CEO, United States Antimony. (SPCX) have gained nearly 10% from their IPO offer price, but Bernstein SocGen Group sees room for a much bigger rally — even without assuming a Tesla merger or SpaceX reaching its full revenue ambitions. SPCX shares slipped about 0.4% on Monday, leaving them 9% above their $135 IPO offer price. The research firm raised its price target to $268 from $248, implying an 82% upside from current levels, and maintained an ‘Outperform’ rating. “We raise our SpaceX outlook primarily on terrestrial AI build plans. We believe the case for a multi-trillion dollar valuation rests on success of orbital data centers,” the firm said. Bernstein said computing infrastructure on Earth adds materially to SpaceX’s revenue outlook, while its enterprise and government connectivity business also appears to be outperforming. The firm now forecasts $424 billion in full-year 2028 revenue. That remains below SpaceX’s ambition to reach an annualized revenue pace of $500 billion to $1 trillion by the end of 2027, although Bernstein raised its estimate. The company’s goal refers to its revenue pace exiting 2027, rather than total sales during that year. “And, as we have said, you do not need to go all the way to the company’s plan to make SpaceX attractive,” the firm said. Bernstein also noted that SpaceX is planning its first orbital data-center launches in late 2027, with operations beginning in mid-2028. Flight 15 is expected within weeks, with SpaceX planning to catch both the booster and the ship. Bernstein said the heat shield’s performance on Flight 14 could set up the first Starship reuse on Flight 16. “Reusability is key to making orbital data centers successful,” the firm said. Bernstein sees SpaceX’s terrestrial computing capacity reaching 13 gigawatts by the end of 2027 — five gigawatts above its previous forecast — before climbing to 20 gigawatts in 2028. This would mark a sharp jump from the 1.7 gigawatts SpaceX reported at the end of September. On the recent earnings call, Musk said he was confident the company could add 10 gigawatts in 2027, on top of the 2.5 gigawatts to 3 gigawatts expected online by the end of this year. Additionally, Bernstein said the company’s comments pointed to compute prices above the $30 to $50 per watt level seen in recent deals. The firm raised its pricing assumptions but left them below the company’s expectations, leaving room for further gains. “If the company achieves its pricing expectations, there could be more upside, both for terrestrial and orbital,” Bernstein said. Bernstein estimates capex of about $35 billion per gigawatt as SpaceX expands capacity. The company’s earnings call underscored the scale of the spending. CFO Bret Johnsen said Q3 capex totaled $19.6 billion and forecast another $35 billion to $40 billion in the fourth quarter. The company also pointed to strong returns on the new infrastructure. “At current pricing, new compute deployments are generating a payback of less than a year,” Johnsen said. SpaceX’s superintelligence segment generated $7.6 billion in third-quarter revenue, making it the company’s largest revenue segment. Bernstein’s model includes neither a potential Tesla merger nor a reported telecom-tower deal. “Elon talked of a possible Tesla merger and SpaceX is reportedly discussing a telco tower deal,” the firm said. “We make no assumptions on either here.” Separately, ARK Investment Management said that combining the companies could allow Tesla’s potential robotaxi cash generation to help fund SpaceX’s expansion. Its no-premium share-swap scenario projected a 3.8-fold increase in returns for Tesla shareholders and a 7.2-fold increase in incremental returns for SpaceX investors. Musk, however, has cautioned that a transaction remains uncertain. Independent board committees, excluding him because of his conflict of interest, have not agreed on terms. “I think some people out there assume that a SpaceX and Tesla merger is a certainty, and I think that would be overstating it,” he said. title: NVIDIA and Meta to Expand Collaboration on Muse and Muse Family of Models Amid Robust Growth - NVIDIA Newsroom
content:
NVIDIA and Meta today announced they will partner to expand their work on Muse and the Muse family of models to improve inference and training performance, reflecting popular demand for useful AI agents. Meta’s Muse models and agents, which leverage NVIDIA’s infrastructure, have delivered frontier-level benchmark performance and surging consumer downloads since launch. Meta and NVIDIA intend to further deepen their collaboration by partnering on optimizations across workflows to maximize performance and improve total cost of ownership. Meta and NVIDIA will also consider additional collaboration opportunities with NVIDIA on its NVIDIA OpenShell Reference Architecture, including NVIDIA OpenShell™ for safe deployment and NVIDIA Sentry for monitoring agent behavior. This announcement reinforces Meta and NVIDIA’s strong long-term partnership to support Meta’s AI infrastructure ambitions. Meta intends to expand the deployment of NVIDIA infrastructure, including Vera Rubin and Vera CPUs for next-generation AI agents to deliver maximum performance per watt. Meta will also deploy NVIDIA Spectrum-X™ Ethernet networking and BlueField-4® to support network efficiency and throughput. In addition, NVIDIA will invest $3 billion in Meta’s equity offering. “AI agents represent a new computing paradigm — software that understands our goals, reasons, uses tools and gets work done on our behalf,” said Jensen Huang, founder and CEO of NVIDIA. “This changes how we use computers, from operating applications to working with intelligent agents. NVIDIA and Meta are expanding our partnership to optimize the computing infrastructure end to end for capable, efficient and secure AI agents, so Muse can empower billions of people to achieve more and pursue greater ambitions.” “Muse is how we bring personal superintelligence to everyone. title: Nasdaq, S&P 500 Futures Gain Premarket While Oil Rebounds: CLS, NVDA, SKHY, CRWV, SOFI In Focus - Stocktwits
content: U.S. stock futures rose early on Tuesday after Wall Street closed higher in the previous session, lifted by artificial-intelligence optimism following Anthropic’s filing for an initial public offering (IPO). As of 5.30 a.m. ET, Nasdaq 100 futures were up 0.11%, while Dow futures rose 0.18% and S&P 500 futures were up 0.1%. Earlier on Monday, the S&P 500 ended 0.7% higher, while the Nasdaq 100 gained 1.1%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average added 0.3%, and the Russell 2000, which tracks small-cap stocks, advanced 0.4%. Investors are now turning their attention to a fresh batch of corporate earnings and the start of the Federal Reserve’s two-day policy meeting. Oil prices initially fell on Tuesday as renewed diplomatic efforts to end the U.S.-Iran war raised hopes of easing tensions across the wider region, where the conflict has also involved Tehran-backed Houthis supporting Saudi Arabia. However, prices later pared their losses and moved into positive territory. By around 5.30 a.m. ET, Brent crude futures had risen 0.47% to $116.36 a barrel, while WTI crude futures gained 0.51% to $102.27 a barrel. Nvidia (NVDA): The company announced a $3 billion investment in Meta Platforms’ (META) equity offering and a partnership to improve Meta’s Muse AI agentic platform. Meta announced a $97.5 billion equity offering on Monday. Later in the day, it said it had sold $12.5 billion in preferred shares at $50 apiece and $25 billion in common stock at $625 per share. META shares traded 0.15% higher in early premarket trading. SK Hynix (SKHY): South Korean newspaper Dong-A Ilbo reported that the memory chipmaker was considering a special dividend of around 16 trillion won ($12 billion). The report came ahead of the company’s third-quarter earnings announcement on Wednesday. Celestica (CLS): Shares of the company jumped nearly 17% in early premarket trading on Tuesday after the data center infrastructure firm posted better-than-expected third-quarter results and signaled strong demand for AI-related infrastructure. Revenue soared 83% year on year to $5.83 billion, beating analyst estimates of $5.47 billion. Adjusted earnings per share more than doubled to $3.30, ahead of the $2.96 consensus forecast CoreWeave (CRWV): Shares were up 1.3% in premarket trading on Tuesday, recovering from a sharp sell-off the previous session. The stock hit a 52-week low on Monday as concerns over the neocloud sector mounted. Pressure intensified after Elon Musk said SpaceX would not acquire neocloud companies, calling such a move “pointless.” CoreWeave shares subsequently rebounded, finishing the session nearly 2% higher. SoFi Technologies (SOFI): Shares fell 0.21% in premarket trading ahead of the fintech company’s third-quarter results, due before the market opens on Tuesday. Analysts expect revenue of $1.26 billion, up 32% from $949.63 million in the same quarter last year, according to Fiscal.ai. Earnings per share are expected to rise to $0.17 from $0.11 a year earlier. Broadcom (AVGO): Shares rose 1.35% in early premarket trading. Broadcom and a consortium of major Wall Street financial institutions announced a $63 billion financing arrangement on Monday to supply hardware to AI startup Anthropic. The consortium includes Bank of America (BAC), Blackstone (BX), Citigroup (C) and Morgan Stanley (MS). The funding will support the acquisition of hardware needed to train and run next-generation AI models. PayPal Holdings Inc. (PYPL): The stock was down 0.38% in early premarket trading ahead of the payments company’s first-quarter results, due before the bell. Analysts expect revenue of $8.71 billion, up from $8.42 billion in the comparable quarter last year, according to Fiscal.ai. Earnings per share are forecast at $1.31, down from $1.34 a year earlier. Uber Technologies (UBER): Shares were up 0.12% in premarket trading on Tuesday. Early Uber investor Jason Calacanis disclosed $1 million purchases in both Uber and Tesla, with his price targets implying around 85% upside for the ride-hailing company, compared with 40% for Tesla from their respective entry prices. Other tickers trending on Stocktwits at the time of writing included Baidu Inc (BIDU), Celestica Inc. (CLS) and Trump Media & Technology Group Corp. (DJT). Investors will track a fresh batch of third-quarter earnings, with Boeing (BA), PayPal Holdings (PYPL), SoFi Technologies (SOFI) and Coca-Cola (KO) scheduled to report before the opening bell. Robinhood (HOOD) and Visa (V) are among the companies due to report after the market closes. The Federal Reserve will also begin its latest two-day policy meeting. While the central bank is widely expected to leave interest rates unchanged, investors will look for clues about its next move and whether another rate hike remains possible before the end of the year. Retail sentiment on Stocktwits remained weak across major index-tracking ETFs. Sentiment toward the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY), which tracks the S&P 500, remained ‘bearish’ over the past 24 hours. The Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ), which tracks the Nasdaq 100, continued to see ‘extremely bearish’ sentiment, unchanged over the same period. Meanwhile, sentiment toward the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (DIA) also remained ‘bearish.’ Also read: Michael Burry Says Anthropic’s IPO Filing Changes Nothing About His AI Bear Case — Flags Financial Risks Beyond The Tech For updates and corrections, email newsroom[at]stocktwits[dot]com Comments posted here will also appear on symbol pages. Dollar General Corp. (DG) stock is drawing attention after the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) and 20 states sued the discount retailer over alleged deceptive pricing practices. The complaint claims stores repeatedly charged customers more than advertised prices, causing millions of dollars in overcharges. Dollar General stock declined 3% on Monday. The stock has been down for the past two weeks. The federal lawsuit claims Dollar General stores repeatedly charged shoppers more at checkout than the prices advertised on shelves, labels, and promotional materials. The complaint says Dollar General kept making pricing mistakes even after customers raised concerns and the company knew about the problem. The FTC and the states claim the retailer failed to take proper steps to stop or fix the errors. “Dollar General has betrayed the trust of millions of American consumers and imposed significant financial harm on communities and consumers who are already struggling to make their paychecks last,” said Christopher Mufarrige, Director, FTC’s Bureau of Consumer Protection. “The FTC’s action underscores the agency’s commitment to lowering costs for consumers by stopping deceptive pricing practices that harm AmerDollar General operates more than 21,000 locations across the U.S. and attracts customers with low-priced household essentials. The FTC and the 20 states contend that the alleged conduct violates the FTC Act, the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act and applicable state laws. The states involved are Alabama, Arizona, Arkansas, California, Connecticut, Florida, Illinois, Iowa, Kansas, Louisiana, Michigan, Mississippi, Nebraska, New Jersey, North Carolina, Ohio, Oklahoma, Tennessee, Utah and Wisconsin. The FTC approved the filing in a unanimous 2-0 vote. The case was brought before the U.S. District Court for the Middle District of Tennessee. Earlier on Monday, JPMorgan analyst Matthew Boss raised Dollar General’s price target to $178 from $176 and maintained an ‘Overweight’ rating, implying a 38% upside from the stock’s last close. The firm also added the stock to its Analyst Focus List and increased its third-quarter estimates after research showed that lower-income shoppers continued to spend steadily. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around the stock remained ‘bearish.’ The stock saw a 650% surge in message volume over the past week. Angel investor Jason Calacanis, an early investor in Uber (UBER) and Robinhood (HOOD), told his followers to sell Bitcoin (BTC) and invest in artificial intelligence on Tuesday, but said he was long Bittensor (TAO). Bitcoin's rough stretch was just getting started, the All-In podcast co-host wrote on X. "A brutal year for Bitcoin is just getting started," he wrote. Calacanis said Bitcoin could revisit its 2026 low within a year. "We will test the 57k low again in the next 12 months," he wrote. He also said Bitcoin "will never break its all-time high again." His argument is that money works best where it grows fastest. Calacanis said there are plenty of faster-growing places for investors to put capital today. He said Bitcoin was a "dead network that offers nothing beyond a store of value". Calacanis said that "The viral nature of bitcoin was it's power... if you didn't own you were MOCKED!" He thinks the promise of changing the world has moved from Bitcoin to AI. He wrote, "Just sell and shift from Bitcoin to Super Intelligence because one provides little to no value, and the other provides unlimited upside for humanity." Calacanis said one telling sign was the Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs). "Outflows from ETFs are signal and will continue," he wrote. According to data from SoSoValue, U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs saw net outflows amounting to $635.6 million on Oct. 22. That was the largest one-day withdrawal since June 25. The selling didn't last. The funds attracted $110.34 million on Monday, ending two straight sessions of outflows, data from SoSoValue showed. However, he was not completely rooting against crypto. Calacanis named his AI bet, saying, “I am long $TAO and love Bittensor’s focus on scaling AI.” Bittensor is a decentralized network that uses TAO to reward machine learning algorithms that offer AI services. TAO’s price edged up over 0.2% at the time of writing. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around TAO dropped to ‘extremely bearish’ from the ‘bearish’ zone, with chatter around it at ‘normal’ levels over the past day. According to platform data, message volume around Bittensor has increased over 60% in a week. On Stocktwits, Bitcoin was among the top trending tickers at the time of writing. Bitcoin’s price was trading around $79,680, down 0.3% in the last 24 hours. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around Bitcoin remained in the ‘bearish’ zone, accompanied by ‘normal’ chatter levels over the past day.  According to platform data, message volume around Bitcoin has increased over 28% over the past week. The biggest upgrade to Bitcoin this year was to the software that most people use to run the network. Introduced in April, it modifies how the network organizes the queue of transactions awaiting processing. That should make it more orderly to decide which payments go through next, and replace a stuck payment with a higher-fee version. The update also added an optional way to send payments more privately. July saw a smaller follow-up that fixed bugs. The clearest first-hand record this year for Bittensor is not about the network itself. According to Grayscale's filing, its Bittensor fund increased its holdings from 36,193 to 38,289.6 TAO in the first quarter, and TAO's price rose from around $220 to around $307 during that period alone. However, investors still can't redeem their shares for the token, pending regulatory approval. BTC’s price is down over 9% so far this year, while TAO’s price has gained over 12% year-to-date. UBS and Oppenheimer raised their price targets, citing AI observability demand and potential OpenAI spending. However, Datadog’s premium valuation remains a key risk for investors. UBS analyst Karl Keirstead raised his price target on Datadog to $320 from $280 and maintained a ‘Buy’ rating, implying 14% upside from the stock’s last closing price. The analyst sees AI-related monitoring services contributing more to the company's growth in 2027. Keirstead also highlighted possible higher spending from OpenAI during the second half of this year, which could provide an additional boost to Datadog's business. Last week, reports suggested Datadog is looking to expand its cybersecurity business by acquiring cloud security startup Upwind. Upwind makes software that monitors cloud applications, including AI agents. However, UBS said Datadog’s stock is expensive compared with its expected growth. The company trades at about 17 times its expected 2027 revenue and 57 times its free cash flow. This means the stock could face pressure if growth misses expectations. Oppenheimer also raised its DDOG price target to $330 from $300 and reaffirmed an ‘Outperform’ rating, implying 185% upside. The firm expects the company to deliver results that could exceed Wall Street's revenue expectations. Oppenheimer sees Datadog’s Q3 revenue coming in more than 4% above current consensus estimates. The firm also expressed confidence in Datadog's business and praised management's ability to execute its strategy. Datadog will report Q3 earnings on Nov. 4. ImmunityBio (IBRX) shares rose nearly 1% overnight heading into Tuesday after CNBC host Jim Cramer called it a “very good spec,” citing a wave of biotech acquisitions as the company advances plans to expand the use of its flagship drug, Anktiva, in bladder cancer. IBRX stock closed Monday down about 5% at $7.81, logging its fourth straight session in the red. Cramer backed ImmunityBio as a speculative bet during Monday’s Mad Money Lightning Round, saying it could pay off even when index funds disappoint. “I don’t mind you taking a position in that, because that’s one of those that you could look back and say, you know what? I was in my index funds, they didn’t really do well, but man, did I clean up on a very good spec,” he said. He pointed to biotech takeovers as part of the appeal. “The biotechs are being taken over like mad, you want to be in one,” Cramer said. The call echoes his June stance, when he encouraged investors to limit speculation to one holding. “Let Immunitybio be your speculation,” he said then. Cramer’s takeover pitch follows a string of recent big drugmaker deals. Earlier this month, Viatris agreed to buy Pacira BioSciences for $1.65 billion, with closing expected by year-end. AbbVie completed its $10.9 billion acquisition of Apogee Therapeutics in September, while Eli Lilly agreed in August to acquire Merida Biosciences for up to $2.875 billion, including milestone payments. Cramer’s backing comes ahead of a November readout that could help ImmunityBio bring Anktiva to patients earlier in bladder cancer treatment. Last week, the company finished checking data from a 366-patient trial comparing Anktiva plus BCG with BCG alone in non-muscle invasive bladder cancer, clearing the way for the final analysis. The study focuses on patients receiving BCG-based treatment for the first time. Anktiva’s current approval covers patients whose disease has not responded to BCG. ImmunityBio also plans to submit an application to expand FDA approval in the fourth quarter. The analysis will assess how many patients achieve a complete response, meaning no detectable cancer under the study’s criteria, and how long those responses last. Earlier this month, the FDA expanded ANKTIVA plus BCG’s approval to include patients with BCG-unresponsive non-muscle invasive bladder cancer with papillary-only tumors. That builds on its 2024 approval for disease with carcinoma in situ, with or without papillary tumors. The company also released long-term results this month from a Phase 2/3 study of 100 patients whose cancer had not responded to BCG. It reported a 71% complete response rate, with some responses lasting more than 53 months. Among responders, three-year survival without bladder-removal surgery was 84%. title: Nvidia Stock News (Oct 27, 2026): NVDA Rises 2.4% to $216.00 - Gotrade
content: Gotrade News - Nvidia (NVDA) rose 2.39% to close at $216.00 on Monday, October 26, 2026, in the US session. The day's Nvidia stock news came from two AI funding stories, Anthropic's IPO filing and a plan by Meta Platforms (META) to raise up to $95 billion through stock sales, in which Nvidia indicated interest in buying shares alongside AMD (AMD) and Broadcom (AVGO). Regular-session close on Monday, October 26, 2026, 4:00 p.m. New York time. Stock prices: Yahoo Finance, cross-checked against the closing price on Nasdaq.com. Volume and 30-day average volume: Nasdaq.com. 52-week range: Yahoo Finance daily highs and lows since October 27, 2025. Indices and the 10-year Treasury yield: Yahoo Finance daily closes for the same date. Follow NVDA's latest price on our Nvidia (NVDA) stock price today page. Nvidia opened at $213.11 and traded between $212.61 and $217.75 before closing $3.39 above its session low. Volume came to 90.8 million shares, 14.04% below its average of 105.7 million shares. The stock outpaced the Nasdaq Composite, which rose 0.82% to 26,169.38, by 1.57 percentage points. The S&P 500 gained 0.70% to 7,676.77 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average added 0.28% to 52,361.58, while the US 10-year Treasury yield ended at 4.99%, down 0.2 basis points. Chipmakers moved with Nvidia: AMD rose 2.80% and Broadcom gained 2.33%, while Meta Platforms fell 1.88%. Nvidia closed 11.25% below its 52-week high of $243.37 and 31.49% above its 52-week low of $164.27. Financial media tied the gain to a rebound in AI-linked chip stocks after two funding announcements on Monday. As reported by TipRanks, Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom rose after Meta announced plans for a stock offering to raise $95 billion for its AI expansion, and after Anthropic filed for an IPO with the SEC. According to Meta's free writing prospectus filed with the SEC on October 26, 2026, Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom, named as "Cornerstone Investors", indicated an interest in buying up to an aggregate $5.0 billion of Class A common stock in a $22.5 billion common stock offering. title: Nvidia NVDA Stock Rebounds on Chip Sentiment Improving but Data-Centre Risks Remain - FXLeaders
content: Nvidia stock rebounded from $210 as semiconductor sentiment improved, but data-centre power shortages, expensive financing, manufacturing constraints and growing competition raise questions about whether infrastructure spending can sustain demand for advanced processors. Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA) shares recovered above $215 after touching $210 last Friday, regaining some ground following a retreat from a record above $243 earlier this month. The rebound reflects renewed buying interest across the semiconductor sector, supported by expectations that memory shortages and higher prices could persist through 2027. However, the recovery comes as investors increasingly question the financial returns from expanding computing infrastructure. Rising borrowing costs, expensive equipment and electricity constraints are complicating the expansion plans of major technology companies. Nvidia remains a leading supplier of advanced processors, but its growth increasingly depends on customers having the financial resources, electricity and infrastructure required to deploy the hardware they purchase. Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN) is reportedly purchasing billions of dollars in Nvidia hardware, yet some server racks are sitting in warehouses because data centres lack sufficient electricity to operate them, according to Business Insider. Internal emails reportedly indicated that Amazon expected to receive $5 billion in Nvidia server systems in August, followed by another $3 billion monthly. The company also introduced an Early Rack Receipt programme, allowing it to secure equipment before facilities are ready for deployment. Previously, Amazon generally waited until hardware reached its data centres before taking ownership. The revised arrangement helps secure scarce equipment but also exposes the company to storage costs and delays between delivery and commercial use. For Nvidia, this highlights a potential weakness in the infrastructure expansion cycle. Strong orders may support near-term demand, but delayed deployments could postpone returns for customers and influence future purchasing decisions. If electricity shortages persist, technology companies may reconsider the timing and scale of new projects, particularly as infrastructure costs rise. Expectations for higher memory prices have provided some support to semiconductor shares. Dell CEO Michael Dell reportedly warned that memory shortages could worsen in 2027, while analysts at Mizuho and KeyBanc have highlighted the potential for NAND flash prices to increase as demand for computing infrastructure expands. Higher memory prices could benefit manufacturers across the supply chain, but they also increase the cost of building and operating data centres. For Nvidia, the key question is whether customers can maintain their investment plans while absorbing rising expenses for processors, memory, electricity and construction. NVIDIA shares lost momentum early in September after failing to break decisively above the $236 resistance zone, with the rejection sending the stock back below $210 but we have seen a decent rebound recently. Shares have climbed above $233 today as investors responded positively to expanding infrastructure partnerships and CEO projections, but buyers are not able to sustain the rally above $243 and we saw dive to $210 again last week but we’re seeing some improvement this week. ASML reported record third-quarter sales of €11.7 billion but warned that planned semiconductor manufacturing capacity in 2027 and 2028 might not fully meet anticipated demand. The company forecast fourth-quarter revenue of €14.2 billion to €15.2 billion and narrowed its 2026 sales guidance to €44 billion–€45 billion. Despite these figures, its U.S.-listed shares reportedly fell approximately 4%, adding pressure to Nvidia and AMD. Manufacturing constraints could support semiconductor pricing, but they may also delay the equipment needed to expand production. This creates a difficult balance for the industry: demand remains strong, yet supply limitations could restrict growth. Financing concerns have intensified following heavy selling in CoreWeave (NASDAQ: CRWV). Yields on its $1.25 billion bond issue due in 2032 reportedly reached 15% before closing near 14.5%, signalling substantial investor concern about credit risk. Such borrowing costs raise questions about the sustainability of debt-financed data-centre expansion. If infrastructure operators face increasingly expensive financing, some projects could be delayed or scaled back, weakening future demand for Nvidia processors. Reported financing discussions involving major technology companies further illustrate the substantial capital required to sustain the industry’s expansion. Microsoft’s Maia 300 processor adds another competitive risk. The chip reportedly targets 40% more tokens per megawatt than leading GPU systems, while a 96-accelerator configuration is designed to deliver up to seven times the rack-scale throughput of its predecessor. Custom silicon could help cloud providers improve efficiency and reduce dependence on external suppliers for selected workloads. Nvidia’s established software ecosystem and broad customer base remain important advantages, but increasingly capable alternatives could eventually pressure its pricing power and market share in specific applications. Questions about OpenAI’s revenue have renewed scrutiny of technology-sector spending assumptions. Its annualised revenue run rate was reportedly around $50 billion at the end of September, below the widely circulated $68 billion figure, which reportedly included revenue generated by partners. The distinction matters because investors need evidence that the commercial demand supporting infrastructure investment can justify its enormous costs. If revenue growth fails to keep pace with spending, technology companies could face pressure to reduce capital expenditure, potentially affecting future processor orders. Nvidia’s rebound above $215 provides some relief after the retreat from $243, but the recovery remains vulnerable to renewed selling. The ability to sustain gains will depend partly on whether major customers can overcome electricity constraints, secure financing and generate sufficient returns from their infrastructure investments. For now, memory shortages and continued demand for advanced processors support the bullish case. However, rising financing costs, manufacturing bottlenecks and competition from custom chips create significant risks. Nvidia’s long-term growth prospects remain substantial, but the sustainability of its rally increasingly depends on whether customers can turn expensive computing infrastructure into profitable businesses.

content: Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA) closed Friday at $210.96, down -0.59%, marking its lowest close in 20 trading days. This came after Thursday’s decline of 4.40% to $212.21, which saw chip stocks and the Nasdaq weighed on by selling pressure. Today, Nvidia has a market cap of $5.09 Trillion. The drop on Thursday was driven by investor concerns about AI spending and financing pressures. Meta fell after its earnings report, while Nvidia slipped again on Friday even as other big names like Micron, AMD, and Intel recovered. Jensen Huang said demand from neocloud companies remains strong, but capital is scarce. This remains the prime worry for investors. Although there is still demand, financing the AI buildout is growing increasingly difficult. The pressure is coming from crude oil above $100, as well as strong bond yields. In the meantime, CNBC announced that Apple will become the market-cap leader after Nvidia. However, OpenAI has reached near $30 Billion funding round at a $1.25 Trillion valuation, showing that investment in AI is still ongoing. Nvidia reported fiscal Q2 revenue of $96.22 Billion, up +106% from previous year. Non-GAAP EPS came in at $2.22, above the analysts’ expectations of $2.10. For Q3, management expects revenue of $108 Billion, plus or minus 2%. The company also anticipates a revenue increase of 70% for fiscal 2028. One estimate suggests Nvidia’s P/E is the lowest it has been in seven years. These figures do suggest the growth outlook, but investors are now looking at the financing of AI spending more carefully. CFO Colette Kress says Q3 gross margin will be around 74%, then could dip to 71% or 72% in Q4. In fiscal 2028, margins are forecasted to recover to 72% to 73% with the increase in prices. However, any decline below this outlook could put added pressure on the stock as investors are reassessing its valuation. On October 16, Nvidia revealed that its RTX Spark laptops were available at the price starting from $2,599. They offer systems from Asus, Dell, HP, Lenovo, Microsoft and MSI. The chip can support up to 128GB of unified memory, and interestingly, it is Nvidia’s first consumer PC chip with full integration. This is an additional revenue stream for NVDA along with the data center sales, which accounted for $89 Billion in Q2 and are still the primary business driver. The RSI of NVDA is 38.2, which indicates an oversold status. Nvidia is trading below its 20-DMA, $225.54, and 50-DMA, $222.48. Shares are down 6.27% over the past month. The first support level to watch will be Friday’s low at $210.18. Wall Street is currently bullish on Nvidia. S&P Global data shows 62 analysts rate the stock a Strong Buy, with an average price target of $328.72 and range between $180 and $515. On October 22, Morgan Stanley repeated its Buy rating and its $300 price target; Citi held on to its $315 price estimate. Earlier this month, BNP Paribas upgraded its price target to $345. For now, a close above $225 would help improve the technical outlook. But a price dip below $210 could open the door to the $200 area. Nvidia is expected to report earnings on November 18, although the company has not confirmed the date. Investors will be looking to see if the company can achieve its $108 Billion revenue guidance, as well as any changes to financing terms for AI infrastructure companies. The shares of Nvidia, a major force in the artificial intelligence sector, fell due to growing investor worries about the spending of AI firms, financing expenses and whether smaller AI companies will be able to fund their infrastructure growth. The weakening in the chip industry compounded the issue. The mean of the analysts’ price estimates is $328.72, while the range is from $180 to $515. Nvidia settled Friday at $210.96, continuing its pullback amid worries over AI financing. Revenue growth continues to be strong, though investors are waiting to see if customers can continue their spending and if margins will be as expected. title: Jensen Huang Says Nvidia's Next-Gen Vera Rubin Chips Will Generate $40 Billion in Revenue per Gigawatt, Up From $25 Billion for Grace Blackwell. What That Means for NVDA's Growth Runway. - The Motley Fool
content: Nvidia says each gigawatt of AI capacity is now worth 60% more to it with Vera Rubin, and that could extend its growth runway even if customers don't add more power. Nvidia (NVDA -1.18%) has already made an incredible amount of money selling the powerful chips that drive artificial intelligence (AI). But CEO Jensen Huang believes the company's biggest opportunities are still ahead, and Nvidia's newest technology could help him prove it. The chipmaker's next-generation Vera Rubin architecture is designed to deliver substantially more computing power from the same amount of electricity. That's important for cloud companies that are racing to build AI data centers, where access to power has become a major constraint. But there's another benefit for Nvidia shareholders. Vera Rubin could generate 60% more revenue per gigawatt of computing capacity than its predecessor. And that helps explain why Huang is so confident about Nvidia's growth runway. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Image source: Getty Images. Nvidia's Hopper and Blackwell graphics processing units (GPUs) have been enormously successful with hyperscalers and smaller cloud providers building artificial intelligence computing capacity. But Nvidia isn't simply selling faster GPUs anymore. Its Vera Rubin platform combines Rubin GPUs, Vera central processing units (CPUs), high-speed NVLink connections, networking equipment, and software into a complete AI computing system. NVLink enables processors to communicate and share memory access more efficiently, helping customers complete more computing work without a corresponding increase in electricity consumption. During Nvidia's fiscal second-quarter 2027 earnings call in August, Huang explained how that expanding platform translates into a bigger revenue opportunity. "In the case of Hopper, we were at about $18 billion per gigawatt. For Grace Blackwell, we're at about $25 billion per gigawatt. And for Vera Rubin, it's about $40 billion per gigawatt," he said. "And the productivity is X-factors increase in each generation." That's a 60% increase over Blackwell, even if customers don't build any additional power capacity. And the technology is already moving into the market. Nvidia says Vera Rubin has entered production shipments, with purchase orders from major hyperscalers, AI cloud providers, and equipment manufacturers. Huang predicted last year that AI infrastructure spending could reach $3 trillion to $4 trillion by 2030, and he reiterated that forecast in September. He's also expecting Nvidia to sell twice as many chips in 2027 as in 2026, according to comments he made to reporters in Scotland on Sept. 17. That doesn't necessarily mean Nvidia's revenue will double. Chip volumes and revenue are different measurements, and the $40 billion-per-gigawatt figure represents a potential sales opportunity rather than guaranteed orders. But the underlying business is already growing at an extraordinary pace. Nvidia reported $96.2 billion in revenue for its fiscal second quarter, which ended July 26, up 106% from a year earlier. Data center revenue alone reached $89 billion. Vera Rubin gives Nvidia another way to increase revenue beyond simply selling more GPUs. If customers continue to expand their AI capacity while spending more per gigawatt on Nvidia technology, the company's growth runway could be considerably longer than its already massive size suggests. title: Questions Arise Over Neoclouds’ Operational Stability, Testing NVIDIA’s (NVDA.US) Role as an AI Financier - 富途牛牛
content: NVIDIA (NVDA.US) stated that, as credit markets tighten for its major partners, the company's role as a global financier of AI infrastructure is facing its first major stress test. After launching relevant chips in the early stages of generative AI, NVIDIA began leveraging its financial strength to provide funding support to AI model developers, data center companies, and several so‑called neoclouds (new cloud service providers). CEO Jensen Huang's strategy, in addition to building cutting‑edge technology, also involves offering customers investment and loan assistance to promote broader adoption of the systems. The arrangements include leveraging NVIDIA's investment-grade credit rating to provide guarantees for OpenAI's large-scale projects, enabling the related construction to secure financing at lower interest rates. As of the most recent quarterly financial filing in July, NVIDIA has entered into off-balance-sheet AI cloud agreements or guarantees involving neoclouds totaling $36 billion, and it has also provided up to $105 billion in guarantees for chips, land, and electricity related to OpenAI's plan to build a 10-gigawatt data center in Ohio. The company has also signed $20 billion in future data center leases, which it will subsequently transfer to third parties. Under most transactions, NVIDIA is only liable for payment if the project participants default. David Trainer, founder and CEO of the financial research firm New Constructs, stated that if computing power demand fails to meet the market's extremely high expectations, problems will arise. Market conditions may test NVIDIA's resilience. In NVIDIA's portfolio, neoclouds such as CoreWeave (CRWV.US), Nebius (NBIS.US), and IREN (IREN.US)—all of which continue to burn cash—have all seen their stock prices plunge by at least 30% this month. Among them, the largest, CoreWeave, has seen its credit default swap spread rise above 11%, reflecting that investors must pay higher premiums to guard against default. Other neoclouds backed by NVIDIA are also facing challenges. The company is an investor in Firmus, an Australian AI cloud provider, which abruptly withdrew its IPO plans this month; UK-based Nscale and SB Energy, which is supported by SoftBank, also filed to list in the U.S. in September, but there has been no update on their progress for several weeks. Last week, Jensen Huang reiterated his confidence in the market, telling CNBC that demand for neoclouds is "extremely strong." During an interview with CNBC at the GTC conference in Berlin, Huang noted that what's currently lacking is working capital to support growth, as surging demand across multiple AI sectors has led to a shortage of available capital. NVIDIA has invested in dozens of companies, including substantial stakes in OpenAI and Anthropic. As of the second quarter, its investment portfolio was valued at $99 billion. Investors told CNBC that the market is watching how NVIDIA will use its cash and its $5 trillion market capitalization to deliver more chips to customers, as well as how much risk the company is willing to take. Brian Stutland, portfolio manager at Equity Armor Investments, said that market volatility reflects investors' concerns about business stability. He noted that CoreWeave and other neoclouds enter into long-term contracts; while their earnings reports appear promising, the market is focused on whether these contracts can remain stable.
